subject: biology-2
question: When building a **cladogram**, a biologist looks for a **shared derived character** to define each clade. Which of the following is the best example of a shared derived character?

options.text: Hair in mammals, a trait present in all mammals and inherited from their most recent common ancestor.
A backbone in fish and mammals, inherited from a much older ancestor.
Wings in bats and birds, which evolved separately in the two lineages.
A trait found in exactly one species, marking that species as distinct.

explanation: A shared derived character arose in the most recent common ancestor of a clade and is passed to every member, while appearing only in that clade, and hair fits mammals perfectly. B describes a shared ancestral character, which is inherited from an older ancestor and cannot separate mammals from their relatives. C is convergent evolution, not an inherited character at all. D describes an autapomorphy, which marks one species and cannot define a clade of many species.
